full_judgment:
(4) Though the plaintiff claimed that she was a pardanashin lady but the Court of appeal, upon assumption and presumption, illegally held that the plaintiff was not a pardanashin lady. 

 (7) There is a presumption of a registered document under the Registration Act and since the deed in question is a registered deed it is presumed to be correctly executed and registered and since the plaintiff alleges that the gift was obtained by misrepresentation the burden was upon the plaintiff to prove her case but she failed to do so and accordingly, the Court of appeal rightly held that the deed of gift was a genuine document. 

 19. To make the disposition by a pardanashin lady a valid one it must be proved that the disposition was substantially understood and it was really the mental act of the person who made it. The rule of law as indicated above is an exception of general rules. The rule of law has been codified in section 111 of the Evidence Act, which provides that where there is a question as to the good faith of a transaction between the parties, one of whom stands to the other in a position of active confidence, the burden of proving the good faith of the transaction is on the party who is in a position of active confidence. Relationship between the pardanashin woman and the person in fiduciary relationship, who is the donee, raises the presumption of influence upon the pardanashin lady and the burden is upon the donee to show that the act was spontaneous.
